# SimJury

> SimJury is an account-free daily courtroom experience. A player hears a serious case, examines the evidence, and deliberates with eleven authored jurors in about twenty minutes. An optional live-jury beta lets invited people join the same room alongside the clearly labelled authored jurors. The player may record Guilty, Not Guilty, or Undecided / No verdict; the jury may agree or hang.

SimJury is static-first. The interactive Daily Docket requires JavaScript, while its raw HTML contains a non-spoiler description of every phase for text-only clients. Solo progress, notes, verdicts, preferences, and sitting statistics stay in the browser. Optional live rooms use short-lived room state only while invited people deliberate.

## Canonical public pages

- [Home](https://simjury.com/): Product introduction, content notice, and the path into the Daily Docket.
- [The Daily Docket](https://simjury.com/today/): Today's featured sitting, the complete seven-case library, evidence, authored or optional live-human deliberation, jury result, reveal, and sharing.
- [Privacy](https://simjury.com/privacy/): Browser storage, short-lived live-room data, narration requests, static delivery, and the absence of accounts, tracking, and runtime AI.

## Site access

- [Complete machine-readable site guide](https://simjury.com/llms-full.txt): Detailed route, interaction, accessibility, privacy, and architecture inventory.
- [XML sitemap](https://simjury.com/sitemap.xml): Canonical public HTML pages.
- [Robots policy](https://simjury.com/robots.txt): Search indexing and user-directed AI retrieval are allowed on public pages. Model-training crawling is not permitted.

## Boundaries

These crawl guides do not reproduce or link case-specific facts, case answers, reveal spoilers, hidden juror state, or source JSON. The former app and installer were removed. `/play/` and `/install/` are legacy redirects, not separate public products.
